stages.title: Foundations & deliberate prompting
stages.description: Turn vague requests into observable, testable work.
stages.outcome: Produce a measured prompt baseline and clear task contracts.

stages.title: Context engineering
stages.description: Select, retrieve, preserve and challenge the information an agent sees.
stages.outcome: Build an evidence packet and durable context handoff.

stages.title: Tools, MCP & skills
stages.description: Design interfaces that make useful actions explicit and bounded.
stages.outcome: Specify tools, trace an MCP interaction and package a reusable skill.

stages.title: Agentic development
stages.description: Use agents to change software through small verifiable increments.
stages.outcome: Deliver a reviewed feature with tests and an evidence trail.

stages.title: Harness engineering
stages.description: Build the runtime that turns model proposals into controlled work.
stages.outcome: Implement state, recovery, budgets and observable execution.

stages.title: Evaluation & reliability
stages.description: Measure outcomes, expose failure modes and make defensible comparisons.
stages.outcome: Create a versioned evaluation suite and release decision.

stages.title: Multi-agent systems
stages.description: Delegate only when coordination produces measurable value.
stages.outcome: Run isolated specialists and evaluate their combined output.

stages.title: Production & capstone
stages.description: Operate, govern and demonstrate a complete system.
stages.outcome: Defend a production plan and portfolio-grade capstone.

lessons.title: Think in systems, then choose the smallest useful agent
lessons.summary: Map Signal Desk from a customer ticket to a verifiable support draft before choosing any model or framework.
objectives: Distinguish model, workflow, agent, tool and harness.
Identify which decisions require judgment and which belong in code.
Define one useful outcome and a baseline.

quiz.question: What belongs to the harness?
options: Context preparation, execution controls, state and validation
quiz.explanation: The harness is the surrounding runtime that turns model proposals into observable, controlled work.

lessons.title: Write task contracts that survive ambiguity
lessons.summary: Replace vague prompting with explicit inputs, constraints, evidence rules and outputs you can check.
objectives: Write a compact task contract with an uncertainty path.
Use examples to clarify decision boundaries.
Separate instruction quality from output fluency.

quiz.question: What is the strongest response to missing diagnostic evidence?
options: Specify missing facts and an appropriate next question
Add a more impressive role description
Force a category and omit uncertainty
quiz.explanation: An explicit uncertainty path preserves usefulness without treating guesses as facts.

lessons.title: Run prompt experiments without fooling yourself
lessons.summary: Use controlled comparisons to discover whether a prompt revision improves Signal Desk rather than merely looking better.
objectives: Separate development cases from held-out cases.
Compare prompts using a fixed rubric and paired cases.
Record uncertainty and avoid premature performance claims.

quiz.question: After repeatedly tuning against your held-out set, what should you do?
options: Treat it as development data and obtain a new final set
quiz.explanation: Repeated tuning consumes the independence of the held-out set.

lessons.title: Design an evidence packet with provenance
lessons.summary: Construct the smallest useful context packet and make every important claim traceable to its source.
objectives: Classify instructions, evidence, assumptions and state.
Preserve provenance and freshness in a compact packet.
Resolve conflicting sources without erasing uncertainty.

quiz.question: A newer document conflicts with a version-specific policy. What matters?
options: Whichever statement is easier to answer
Applicability, authority and provenance as well as freshness
quiz.explanation: Freshness does not establish that a document applies to the same product version or has authority.

lessons.title: Retrieve evidence before generating answers
lessons.summary: Build a small retrieval experiment that exposes why finding a document and supporting a claim are different tasks.
objectives: Create a lexical retrieval baseline and measure recall.
Choose chunks that preserve exceptions and identifiers.
Audit whether citations actually support generated claims.

quiz.question: A draft cites a real document. What is still required?
options: Check that the cited passage supports the specific claim
quiz.explanation: Source existence and claim support are different checks.

lessons.title: Make memory resumable, inspectable and forgettable
lessons.summary: Preserve useful progress across sessions without turning stale summaries into permanent truth.
objectives: Design a handoff that supports safe resumption.
Separate durable facts from working hypotheses.
Specify invalidation and deletion rules for stored context.

quiz.question: What should a resuming agent do first with a completion claim in memory?
options: Trust it because it was summarized
Verify the referenced artifacts and current evidence
quiz.explanation: A summary can be stale or inconsistent; observable artifacts establish current state.

lessons.title: Design tools as precise contracts
lessons.summary: Build tool interfaces that make the right operation obvious and invalid operations easy to reject.
objectives: Define tool inputs, outputs, errors and side effects.
Distinguish read operations from proposed mutations.
Test tool contracts independently of a model.

quiz.question: A save-draft tool returns success. What can the agent conclude?
options: The specific documented local write succeeded
quiz.explanation: Tool success supports only the side effect defined by that tool contract.

lessons.title: Understand MCP by tracing one request
lessons.summary: Learn where MCP fits by following discovery, a tool call and its result through a local Signal Desk integration.
objectives: Distinguish host, client and server responsibilities.
Trace discovery and execution without confusing transport with policy.
Design a protocol-shaped offline simulator and failure cases.

quiz.question: Does discovering a tool establish permission to execute it?
options: Yes, if its description sounds safe
No; host and server policy still govern execution
quiz.explanation: Discovery describes available capabilities; authorization and validation remain separate controls.

lessons.title: Package a skill that improves repeatable work
lessons.summary: Turn a successful Signal Desk procedure into a discoverable, testable skill with a clear activation boundary.
objectives: Write skill metadata that identifies when the procedure applies.
Separate concise instructions from supporting references.
Test activation, execution and non-activation cases.

quiz.question: What is the best evidence that a skill is reusable?
options: It works from its files on new cases without hidden chat context
quiz.explanation: A reusable procedure must transfer to new cases with explicit dependencies and completion criteria.

lessons.title: Turn a feature request into a bounded coding task
lessons.summary: Give an agent a change request that defines behavior, boundaries and verification without dictating every implementation detail.
objectives: Translate a user need into acceptance examples.
Scope a change using repository evidence.
Write an implementation brief with meaningful verification.

quiz.question: What should define a coding task before implementation?
options: Observable before/after behavior and acceptance cases
The number of files to create
quiz.explanation: Behavior and acceptance cases give implementation and review a shared target.

lessons.title: Use verification loops that catch real defects
lessons.summary: Drive a coding change with independent checks and learn why an agent saying its work is correct is not evidence.
objectives: Write behavioral tests that can fail for the right reason.
Use failures to guide one bounded repair at a time.
Distinguish assertions about behavior from implementation mirroring.

quiz.question: Why test an always-successful mutant?
options: To verify that tests can detect a validator that rejects nothing
quiz.explanation: A suite that passes an always-successful validator cannot establish rejection behavior.

lessons.title: Review AI changes through evidence and failure paths
lessons.summary: Perform a review that follows data, authority and state through the patch, then deliver a clear account of what changed.
objectives: Review a patch against requirements and failure behavior.
Identify unsupported completion claims and hidden scope changes.
Write a delivery note with concrete verification and limits.

quiz.question: What makes a review finding actionable?
options: A broad warning without an example
A statement that AI code is risky
A trigger, consequence and evidence pointing to the defect
quiz.explanation: Actionable findings show how the defect occurs and why it matters.

lessons.title: Build the agent loop as an explicit state machine
lessons.summary: Turn model proposals into a bounded execution loop with clear transitions and useful terminal outcomes.
objectives: Separate proposal, validation, execution and observation.
Define terminal states and enforce an iteration budget.
Replay a loop using scripted responses before adding a model.

quiz.question: Who should enforce the maximum number of steps?
quiz.explanation: Runtime enforcement remains effective even when the planner ignores or misunderstands its instructions.

lessons.title: Recover from crashes without duplicating work
lessons.summary: Design checkpoints and idempotent operations so interruption becomes a recoverable state rather than a mystery.
objectives: Identify crash windows around writes and checkpoints.
Use operation IDs to reconcile uncertain outcomes.
Distinguish retryable failures from unresolved side effects.

quiz.question: A write times out after it may have succeeded. What is the correct interpretation?
options: Its outcome is uncertain until reconciled or safely deduplicated
Retry immediately with a new operation ID
quiz.explanation: A missing response does not establish whether the side effect occurred.

lessons.title: Make cost, latency and behavior observable
lessons.summary: Instrument the harness so you can explain what happened, where time went and why a run stopped.
objectives: Design a trace that correlates steps, tools and outcomes.
Enforce separate step, time and cost budgets.
Minimize sensitive data while preserving diagnostic value.

quiz.question: Why distinguish budget exhaustion from task failure?
options: It makes success rates look better
Budget exhaustion describes a runtime limit, not proof the task is impossible
Only the model can tell them apart
quiz.explanation: A bounded run can stop before resolving an otherwise solvable task; reporting the reason supports recovery.

lessons.title: Build an evaluation set that reflects the job
lessons.summary: Create a versioned benchmark with meaningful coverage, defensible labels and explicit limits.
objectives: Design cases around risks and real decision boundaries.
Separate dataset splits and preserve label provenance.
Handle ambiguous cases without manufacturing certainty.

quiz.question: What should a label specify for a generative support draft?
options: Acceptable behavior, required evidence and forbidden claims
quiz.explanation: Behavioral labels allow valid wording variation while preserving the requirements that matter.

lessons.title: Use graders carefully and report uncertainty
lessons.summary: Combine deterministic checks, human judgment and optional model graders without confusing a score with truth.
objectives: Choose the right grader for each requirement.
Calibrate subjective judgments against reviewed examples.
Report paired outcomes, severe failures and sample limitations.

quiz.question: A candidate improves average score but introduces an unauthorized-action failure. What should you do?
options: Inspect the severe regression and apply the release policy
Change the grader to pass it
quiz.explanation: Averages cannot override explicit critical failure constraints.

lessons.title: Red-team the whole system and set release gates
lessons.summary: Test how failures cross boundaries, then define a release decision that remains meaningful under pressure.
objectives: Design attacks against data, tools, state and evaluation.
Trace defenses to concrete enforcement points.
Create release gates that combine usefulness and critical constraints.

quiz.question: What is a strong release response to a critical tool-boundary failure?
options: Fix it or remove the affected capability and verify the narrower scope
Ask the model to be more careful
quiz.explanation: A concrete capability change or verified repair addresses the failure; presentation changes do not.

lessons.title: Decide when delegation is worth its coordination cost
lessons.summary: Use multiple agents where tasks can be separated and verified, then compare the result with a simpler baseline.
objectives: Identify independently executable subtasks.
Write worker contracts with bounded context and outputs.
Estimate coordination cost before adding specialists.

quiz.question: Which work is best suited to parallel delegation?
options: Tasks that all edit the same file without coordination
A strict dependency chain with no independent work
Independent subtasks with explicit inputs and verifiable outputs
Anything, if enough agents are available
quiz.explanation: Independence and clear contracts reduce coordination cost and integration risk.

lessons.title: Coordinate workers without losing ownership or state
lessons.summary: Design handoffs, ownership and conflict resolution so parallel work produces a coherent result.
objectives: Define a parent-worker protocol and artifact ownership.
Handle stale outputs, timeouts and duplicate messages.
Integrate conflicting findings using evidence and version checks.

quiz.question: A worker returns an older policy version after a newer result was accepted. What should happen?
options: Overwrite the final result because it arrived last
Detect the version mismatch and reconcile or reject automatic integration
quiz.explanation: Arrival order is not evidence of freshness; input versions determine applicability.

lessons.title: Measure whether your agent team is actually better
lessons.summary: Compare a team with a single-agent baseline using outcome quality, coordination failures and total resource use.
objectives: Construct a fair paired comparison of team and baseline.
Measure coordination overhead and correlated mistakes.
Choose an architecture based on observed tradeoffs.

quiz.question: Three workers agree using the same mistaken source. What does their agreement establish?
options: Only shared agreement; the evidence can still be wrong
That the minority should always be ignored
quiz.explanation: Correlated evidence and assumptions can produce unanimous error.

lessons.title: Design a production boundary and service contract
lessons.summary: Translate a successful local prototype into a scoped operating plan with ownership, reliability targets and controlled rollout.
objectives: Define users, deployment scope and service-level indicators.
Separate application permissions from model behavior.
Plan staged rollout, fallback and rollback with measurable triggers.

quiz.question: What makes a service indicator meaningful?
options: A clear user-relevant event, denominator and measurement window
quiz.explanation: Explicit definitions prevent misleading comparisons and hidden failures.

lessons.title: Operate the system and learn from incidents
lessons.summary: Practice diagnosis, containment and learning so failures improve the system instead of becoming repeated surprises.
objectives: Triage incidents using traces and observable impact.
Write a runbook with containment and recovery steps.
Convert an incident into a regression case and ownership changes.

quiz.question: A reviewer confidently blames the model for an incident. What should guide diagnosis?
options: The first observable failing boundary and supporting artifacts
quiz.explanation: Incident diagnosis should follow evidence and distinguish symptoms from contributing causes.

lessons.title: Choose, build and defend your capstone
lessons.summary: Choose the support, QA or research project, then use a shared rubric to defend a reproducible result. The 90-minute clinic precedes 10–20 project hours.
objectives: Deliver one of three bounded AI workflow projects with evidence.
Demonstrate evaluation, adversarial behavior and appropriate recovery.
Defend tradeoffs and define the next justified improvement.

quiz.question: What makes the capstone credible?
options: Many agents and a dramatic demo
A claim of production readiness without deployment
Reproducible behavior, failure evidence, clear scope and honest limits
quiz.explanation: Credibility comes from reviewable outcomes and evidence, including the system’s limits.
